feed.title: NPR Topics: World
feed.subtitle: NPR world news, international art and culture, world business and financial markets, world economy, and global trends in health, science and technology. Subscribe to the World Story of the Day podcast and RSS feed.

entry.title: The College of Magic turns ordinary kids into confident, top-hat wearing magicians
entry.summary: The students, many from marginalized communities, learn to conjure up candy, do card tricks — and face the world with a confident, creative and resilient mindset.

entry.title: Soldiers guard center of Milan as thousands of protesters march in cities across Europe
entry.summary: While protests in France have claimed most international attention, large demonstrations also rocked many European cities Saturday from Milan to Rome to Madrid, Lisbon and Tirana.

entry.title: Protests roil France once again as police seek to quell violence
entry.summary: Hundreds of thousands turned out across France to protest everything from the lack of school funding to economic inequality. Police also were out in force to prevent a repeat of last week's violence.

entry.title: Why a far-right cabinet minister in Israel has Netanyahu's ear
entry.summary: Israel's most far-right cabinet minister helped dictate hardline policies toward Palestinians in recent years. Benjamin Netanyahu vows to give him a senior position if Netanyahu is reelected next week.

entry.title: Ukraine says Starlink is back to normal after disruptions
entry.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said that normal Starlink operating speeds were restored after more than a week of disruptions.

entry.title: Gunmen open fire at a church during a funeral in Jordan, killing 7 and wounding 40
entry.summary: Footage broadcast on Jordanian state television showed three gunmen firing shots at a Greek Orthodox church in the city of Karak on Friday.

entry.title: European student protests take aim at Serbia's elections
entry.summary: Students have been protesting across Europe. In Serbia, they've selected candidates to run for parliament in Sunday's elections. And they're aiming to end 14 years of government by the populist leader Aleksandar Vucic.

entry.title: Drinking water supplies dwindle in Yemeni city besieged by Houthi rebels
entry.summary: Taiz, a city in southwestern Yemen, faces a severe water crisis as Houthi rebels backed by Iran tighten their encirclement. The city has struggled with water issues for over a decade, but the situation has worsened in recent weeks.

entry.title: Israeli PM pledges massive military operation after West Bank checkpoint attack
entry.summary: Israel's Prime Minister is vowing to launch a major military operation in the West Bank in response to an attack by two Palestinian gunmen on an Israeli military checkpoint that killed two soldiers.

entry.title: Authorities investigating whether first Kenya and Nigeria Ebola cases crossed paths
entry.summary: Nigeria this week recorded its first case of Ebola in the current outbreak, which has spread from the epicenter in Congo to several other African countries.
